issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**: `CleanupNodes` currently enlists all nodes and deletes *all* of them. This is unintuitive as each node preparer should probably only cleanup the nodes it created.

/sig scheduling
/sig testing
/assign

review_comments:
I'm not fully familiar with this test , but in Line108 it lists all the nodes again ...

My question is, why the test intersect with other nodes and is not properly isolated? it sounds weird that an integration test create nodes in paralell with other tests, usually each tests creates its own apiserver with its own etcd shard, that guarantees its independence ... and everything is destroyed on shutdown

Currently we may have multi IntegrationTestNodePreparer instances in one cluster, so functionally, they should only cleanup the nodes created by themself. I wouldn't say this is a  bad design, but maintaining only one manager sounds better.

This is based on my current understanding. I just visit these codes recently.

> Currently we may have multi IntegrationTestNodePreparer instances in one cluster

Do we? It sounds like something that shouldn't be allowed. So we could produce a fatal if we create more than one.

Yea, @kerthcet is correct. `IntegrationTestNodePreparer` is created every time `createNodesOp` is operated and it works.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8287e21228e9b1c945d031581e2fc63920f46d56/test/integration/scheduler_perf/scheduler_perf_test.go#L668

`getNodePreparer` creates `IntegrationTestNodePreparer`
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8287e21228e9b1c945d031581e2fc63920f46d56/test/integration/scheduler_perf/scheduler_perf_test.go#L914

That's why cleaning up only Nodes prepared by that `IntegrationTestNodePreparer` makes sense in the current implementation.

But, yeah, I think using only one `IntegrationTestNodePreparer` and cleaning up all Nodes in a `CleanupNodes` method would be another nice approach. And, actually, I prefer it to the current multiple-`IntegrationTestNodePreparer` implementation.
Thanks @sanposhiho Do we have any plan to refactor this to a singleton object or this is as designed?
oh, commented at the same time 😄

The conclusion is for the current, we may have multi `IntegrationTestNodePreparer` instances, so this PR walks on the right way, just cleaning up the created nodes by its own. 

In the future, we'll refactor the architecture to make `IntegrationTestNodePreparer` a singleton, then we'll cleanup all nodes in this test. But I think it still make sense for the nodes to cleanup are also the created ones.

"we may" or "we do"?

I think the requirement shouldn't be that we call the preparer once. The requirement is that we shouldn't call it again, if we haven't cleaned the nodes first.

I prefer we move in that direction instead of merging this PR.

/hold
we should not have test pollution if we can ...

> "we may" or "we do"?
> 
It depends, if he/she adds multi `createNodesOp` in yaml file, we'll create multi instances. If not, we have only one.

> I think the requirement shouldn't be that we call the preparer once. 

My first design in my mind is that we may instantiate one preparer, and register nodes to the preparer when we call `createNodesOp`, tear down when finished. So I don't care about how many times you call, but we'll have only one manager.

> The requirement is that we shouldn't call it again, if we haven't cleaned the nodes first.

If we can make sure that we'll clean up the nodes created by each preparer instance finally,  it doesn't matter anymore. 

I can think of a case like different node types created by different preparer instances, and we want to keep them both. Then when cleaning up, we only tear down the nodes created by its own.

> we should not have test pollution if we can ...

Absolutely, what test pollution do you mean here, between different tests?
